clue.text: Harmless medicament -put by ten out of box

parts.note: to put something is to place it

indicators.note: the word box loses a letter, the one standing for ten taken out of it

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Instructions for packing a mild medicine, ten tablets taken out of the box and set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put by' reads as setting something aside, but 'put' is the first piece and 'by' just joins; 'out of' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active drug, so it does the patient no harm.

clue.text: Flower set up? Nonsense!

parts.note: a poppy is a flower
to cock something is to set it up, as a hat or an ear is cocked

explanation.surface: A flower arranged in a vase, and someone scoffing at it.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK means raise or tilt up, as in cocking a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppycock is an exclamation meaning rubbish or balderdash.

clue.text: Attack biblical king, in a way

indicators.note: in places the king inside the letters made from a and way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Saul was the first king of Israel

explanation.surface: An Old Testament king launching an attack in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as an idiom, but 'in' is the container signal and 'way' is the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent physical attack.

clue.text: Often dug up in the garden and cooked — the marrow

definitions.text: Often dug up in the garden

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and changed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vegetable grown and harvested from the garden, then cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges THE MARROW; a marrow is a large British squash.
explanation.definitionFit: Worms are turned up whenever a gardener digs the soil.

clue.text: Formerly Conservative taken in by somebody

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the abbreviation sits within the word for somebody

parts.note: one is somebody, as in one who knows
Conservative gives C

explanation.surface: A former Tory politician fooled by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' reads like being fooled; here it puts CON inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past.

clue.text: A lot investing to fit out vessel

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so one word wraps around the other here

parts.note: your lot in life is your fate
to rig a ship is to fit it out with sails and ropes

explanation.surface: Spending a great deal to equip a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' reads like spending money, but it means besieging or enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship, a sea-going craft.

clue.text: Gave notice 'of rising remuneration around the north-east

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around puts the reward word about the compass abbreviation

parts.note: a reward is a payment, remuneration
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: An announcement of a pay rise for workers in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the little word in this down clue; 'around' wraps the payment word about the compass point, giving REWARNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Forewarned means alerted in advance, given a warning.

clue.text: 'Unsettled, Delia Wilde's husband was

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters of the name are moved around

explanation.surface: A woman upset about what her playwright husband was like.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde wrote the play An Ideal Husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Wilde's comedy describes the husband as perfect.

clue.text: Feeling thrilled-it's exhilarating — leastways, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone excited because something is at least partly exhilarating.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'it's', but the definition is only 'Feeling thrilled'; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be atingle is to be tingling with excitement.

clue.text: What editors do right away giving us the bird

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is removed

parts.note: rejection slips said that the editor regrets being unable to publish

explanation.surface: Editors cutting something at once and giving someone the brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Old rejection notes began 'The Editor regrets'; 'giving us the bird' sounds like rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Concerning bribe rejected by model

indicators.note: rejected here means thrown back, so the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for concerning, about
a sop is a small bribe or concession to keep someone quiet

explanation.surface: A model turning down a bribe offered about some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns RESOP round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is someone who poses, as an artist's sitter does.

clue.text: Stays out of his shop

parts.note: reads as a man keeping away from his own premises, but stays are the boned supports of a corset, which come out of this maker's shop

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who never shows up at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are old-fashioned corsets stiffened with whalebone.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker or seller of corsets turns out stays from the workshop.

clue.text: Boys, you'll get this, not I

parts.note: taken as the word you, the 'll is part of the link

indicators.note: not I means the letter I is left out of the word this

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teasing riddle: the boys will understand this, but I won't.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a playful riddle; 'not I' is an instruction to drop the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Youths are young men, lads.

clue.text: Tormented with guilt, being non-U, time of gloom

indicators.note: tormented suggests twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: non-U means without U, so this letter is subtracted from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone racked with guilt, and socially common too, in a dark time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tormented' rearranges WITH GUILT; 'non-U' takes its U away first. Non-U is also British slang for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim half-light of dusk, a gloomy hour.

clue.text: He keeps on talking about chap who's mad on telly

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland
the box is slang for the television

explanation.surface: A man who never stops talking about a fellow obsessed with TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces; telly and box are British words for TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is someone who talks incessantly.

clue.text: Better in the open air or away from it?

indicators.note: the word or is to be taken away from the outdoor word just named

parts.note: outdoor describes being in the open air
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether outdoors or indoors is better.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTDOOR with OR removed leaves OUTDO.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Mechanically driven, like Richard III at Bosworth

explanation.surface: A motor car compared with a king who lost his mount in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard III cries 'A horse! my kingdom for a horse!' at the Battle of Bosworth Field.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseless carriage is an early motor car, and Richard was left without a mount in the battle.

clue.text: Run into trouble with 4 on an 'orse

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts one piece above the next
trouble means stir up or disturb, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer to clue 4 down
a hunter is a horse; dropping the h as in 'orse leaves it without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone getting into difficulty riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns the 4-down answer into ENCO; the dropped H of ''orse' cues a hunter without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to meet them unexpectedly.

clue.text: Sort of sport the Observer goes in for

definitions.text: Sort of sport the Observer goes in for

parts.words: Sort of sport the Observer goes in for
parts.note: reads as a newspaper's sports coverage, but describes the kind of sport people watch rather than play

explanation.surface: A newspaper with a sports section it favours.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday paper, and there is also a weekly magazine with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher at a game is the onlooker who follows events without taking part.

clue.text: Leo confused with Kermit in the distance

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two characters, a lion and a frog, muddled together far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges LEO and KERMIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilometre is a unit of distance, a thousand metres.

clue.text: Album ruined — go and make a complaint

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruined record leads to a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges ALBUM to LUMBA, then GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, a medical ailment.

clue.text: Money talking, though out of sight here

indicators.note: talking means spoken, so the word for money is heard as another

parts.note: cash is money in notes and coins

explanation.surface: Money speaks, even when it is kept hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' means the word is heard, not seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, a place where things are kept concealed.

clue.text: First murderer about ready to play the lead

indicators.note: about says the killer's name goes around the other word

parts.note: Cain killed Abel, the first murder in the Bible
apt means ready or inclined

explanation.surface: An actor in the role of the first killer preparing to take the main part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First murderer' looks like a cast list entry in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To captain a team is to lead it.

clue.text: Herb, left out, flushed and gave a silly grin

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is dropped from the herb's name

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb
red describes a face that has flushed

explanation.surface: Someone who turned pink and smirked about a herb being omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple is an old herbal remedy plant; 'left out' looks like a phrase but splits as the letter and its removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To simper is to smile in an affected, foolish way.

clue.text: Mum with war service-it's not natural

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence
ARP was Air Raid Precautions, the British wartime civil-defence service

explanation.surface: A mother serving in the war being unnatural.
explanation.walkthrough: In music a natural note is neither raised nor lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a raised note is a semitone above natural, not plain.

clue.text: Initially easy access that every new consumer has

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Every new customer gets easy access at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is completed by the answer: a consumer has done it.
explanation.definitionFit: What a consumer has done to food is to have consumed it.

clue.text: Young lap-dog, kept on a string

parts.note: pup is a young dog
a lap-dog is a pet

explanation.surface: A small dog being walked on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a phrase standing for a thing worked on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a figure worked by strings, so it is controlled from above.

clue.text: Ray Wood

explanation.surface: A pair of names, perhaps two people.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray and Wood both look like people's names.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a shaft of light, and also a long piece of timber.

clue.text: A cushion the, wrong way round — with furniture, that can be altered

indicators.note: the word for a cushion is turned to face the wrong way, reading backwards

parts.note: a pad is a cushion
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Rearranging furniture after putting a cushion on backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong way round' gives DAP from the cushion word; 'the' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible can be adjusted or modified for new conditions.

clue.text: Health food

explanation.surface: A two-word heading on a menu for a health food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: One drinks a toast to someone's health.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a drink to someone's well-being, and also browned bread.

clue.text: In the States it's a capital bird

definitions.text: In the States it's a capital

explanation.surface: An American city named after a mythical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The state capital of Arizona shares its name with the mythical bird reborn from ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona's state capital, and the legendary bird that rises from its own ashes.

clue.text: One interrupting Silas, the ancient story-teller

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Silas Marner is George Eliot's weaver, so Silas leads to his surname
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone breaking in on Silas, an old teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner has the old sailor telling his tale to a wedding guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner buttonholes a wedding guest to tell his long tale.
